lines.trans: Straight to the millimetre! Every guest who checks in will see Jasmine Street in gold leaf!
Wait a minute, Ziad—why have you been grinning at your coat pocket for ten minutes?
Because the Municipal Heritage Office asked me to hold one official letter until tonight!
Official letter from City Hall?! Hold on, my heart cannot survive another inspection!
Relax, Mazen—remember that Wednesday heritage report praising Room Nine and your courtyard?
Look at the gold city crest on this cream envelope! Open it quickly, Mazen!
Glasses on my nose—let me read: Invitation to the Amman Historic Courtyard Festival!
THE HISTORIC COURTYARD FESTIVAL?! Five hidden courtyards opening across Amman for one weekend?!
Music, baking, local craft tables, and a golden plaque for the warmest courtyard in town!
Wait—hundreds of visitors walking down Jasmine Street for our piano and Salma and her bread?!
Say yes right now, Mazen—we already have windproof clothespins AND a master map!
Dip the pen in ink, Nour: Jasmine Courtyard House is entering the Historic Courtyard Festival!

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of دافي ('warm'); also spelled أدفا.

examples.trans: The piano's sound is warmer when it rains.
The attic is the warmest room in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: The n-pattern of فتح: the thing opens by itself, nobody is named (الباب انفتح 'the door came open').

examples.trans: The window blew open by itself in the wind.
The old lock does not open easily.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Form V verb (بيتحمّل / تحمّلت). Used for enduring stress, weight, or a surprise inspection.

examples.text: قلبي ما بيتحمّل تفتيش تاني اليوم!
examples.trans: My heart cannot survive another inspection today!
This brick endures rain and heavy weight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تراثية, plural: تراثيين).

examples.trans: He works on restoring heritage buildings in Amman.

examples.text: هاد بيت تراثي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: This is a historic house eighty years old.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Verbal noun of فتّش ('to inspect, check officially').

examples.text: لجنة التفتيش من البلدية جاية يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The inspection team from City Hall is coming on Wednesday.
The whole kitchen is clean and ready for inspection.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for a written or official report (تقرير التراث 'the heritage report'). Plural: تقارير.

examples.text: تقرير البلدية مدح ساحتنا يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The city report praised our courtyard on Wednesday.

examples.text: كتبت تقرير مختصر عن حالة المبنى.
examples.trans: I wrote a brief report on the condition of the building.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for an artisanal craft or profession. Plural: حرف (حرف يدوية 'handicrafts').

examples.text: بالمهرجان في طاولات حرف يدوية حلوة.
examples.trans: At the festival there are lovely local craft tables.

examples.text: رسم الخرايط حرفة بدها صبر ودقة.
examples.trans: Mapmaking is a craft that requires patience and precision.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Active participle of دخل ('to enter'), used like a progressive verb in Arabic (بيت الياسمين داخل على المهرجان 'is entering the festival').

examples.text: بيت الياسمين داخل على مهرجان الساحات!
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is entering the Courtyard Festival!

examples.text: هي سعاد داخلة من باب الساحة.
examples.trans: Look, Suad is coming in through the courtyard door.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of دخل ('to enter'). تسجيل دخول means 'check-in' at a hotel or guesthouse.

examples.text: كل ضيف بيسجل دخول بيشوف الخريطة.
examples.trans: Every guest who checks in will see the map.
Entry to the festival is free for everyone.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a formal or friendly invitation (دعوة لمهرجان 'invitation to a festival'). Plural: دعوات.

examples.trans: An invitation to the Historic Courtyard Festival reached us!
Thank you for your kind invitation to tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Pronounced dahab in Jordanian Arabic (often spelled دهب in dialectal writing). ورق دهب means 'gold leaf'.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين مرسوم بورق دهب دافي.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is painted in warm gold leaf.

examples.text: ساعة الجد فيها إطار ذهب قديم.
examples.trans: Grandfather's watch has an old gold frame.

راح.gloss: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بروح, بيروح).

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: The imperative روق (rawwiq, to a man) or روقي (to a woman) means 'chill, relax'. Related to رايق, calm and in a good mood.

examples.text: روقي يا بنت، لسا في وقت.
examples.trans: Relax, girl, there is still time.
I drink my coffee and relax a bit.

meanings.note: Active participle noun from زار ('to visit'). Everyday plural: زوار ('visitors').

examples.trans: Hundreds of visitors will come to the festival!
The visitor loved the mint tea very much.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسجل, بيسجل).

examples.text: سجلنا بالغلط حجزين على غرفة سبعة!
examples.trans: By mistake we booked two reservations into room seven!
I wrote the name down in the big ledger.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a crest, badge, or emblem (شعار المدينة 'the city crest'). Plural: شعارات.

examples.trans: Look at the gold city crest on the envelope!

examples.text: علّق مشبك الغسيل على جاكيته زي الشعار.
examples.trans: He clipped the clothespin onto his jacket like a badge.

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday Form I verb (بضحك / ضحك) meaning 'to laugh' or 'grin playfully'.

examples.text: ليش عم بتضحك لجيبة الجاكيت تبعتك؟
examples.trans: Why are you grinning at your coat pocket?

examples.text: ضحكنا كلنا لما شفنا النظارة على جبينه.
examples.trans: We all laughed when we saw the glasses on his forehead.

meanings.note: Preposition meaning 'against' or 'resistant to / -proof' (ضد المي 'waterproof', ضد الهوا 'windproof').

examples.trans: We sealed the recipe in waterproof plastic.

examples.text: مشابك الغسيل الخشب ضد الهوا القوي.
examples.trans: The wooden clothespins are proof against strong wind.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from عاج ('ivory'), describing warm cream tones on paper or cloth.

examples.trans: Every envelope has ivory paper.
I chose a cream shirt for the party.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Any time off work or school; in Jordan the weekly break is Friday and Saturday.

examples.trans: Next holiday we are going to Aqaba.
Tomorrow is a day off, there is no work.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The clean sheets are in the linen closet.
We hung the laundry in the morning sun.

meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'dip a sponge in water or dunk bread/biscuits in tea'.

examples.text: غطست الإسفنجة بالمي الدافية ومسحت اللوح.
examples.trans: I dipped the sponge in warm water and wiped the pane.

examples.text: بحب أغطس البسكوت بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I love dipping biscuits in a glass of hot tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Form V active participle widely used in Levantine Arabic instead of a present tense verb for 'I remember' (أنا متذكّر).

examples.trans: I still remember the color of the lantern.
Do you remember the name of the shop?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مخفية, plural: مخفيين).

examples.trans: A hidden door in the cellar is drawn on the map!
The key was hidden inside the box.

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بمدح / مدحت) from root م-د-ح, used when admiring someone's work or cooking.

examples.trans: Everyone praises you at the restaurant.
The guests praised the Arabic coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدن.

examples.trans: Amman is an old, lovely hilltop city.
City law protects public gardens.

meanings.note: Form X active participle from root ق-و-م ('to stand straight'), describing lines, posture, or directions.

examples.trans: Walk straight down the street.
We drew a straight line with the ruler.

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from شبك ('fasten/clip'): names a shutter catch/hook or paper clip.

examples.text: ثبتنا الشيش عالحيط بمشبك حديد أسود ماكن.
examples.trans: We secured the shutter against the wall with a sturdy black iron catch.

examples.text: تأكد إن المشبك مسكر منيح قبل ما تهب الريح.
examples.trans: Make sure the catch is latched tightly before the wind blows.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مغلفات.

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the door.
We opened the thick envelope calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مكاتب.

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مليمترات.

examples.trans: The ring width is twenty millimetres exactly.
He measured the part to the millimetre.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Originally plural of منخار ('nostril'), used universally in Levantine Arabic as the normal word for 'nose'.

examples.trans: He has my exact nose, I swear.
My nose is red from the cold.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (pl. مهرجانات) used for street festivals, fairs, and cultural events.

examples.trans: We should put up a poster for the festival.
The street is full of people during the festival.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of وافق ('to agree'); common as a quick reply: موافق ('deal / agreed').

examples.trans: Agreed, uncle — let's do it.
Everyone agrees on the new idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نهايات.

examples.trans: There is a new booking for the weekend.

examples.text: بالنهاية كل شي انحل على خير.
examples.trans: In the end everything worked out well.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from يد ('hand') using the glide -aw- before -ي; used for crafts and handmade notebooks.

examples.trans: Also the little notebook is handmade.
We love handmade embroidery work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
